text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- MAJORITY IN SAO PAULO WANT CASINOS
A majority of people living in the greater Sao Paulo area favor legalization of gaming casinos, according to a Gallup poll.
-- YEAR ENDS AND CONGRESS HAS NOT YET PASSED REFORMS
The legislative year comes to an end this Friday and the government has failed to get Congress to pass pension, administrative and tax reforms, all of which have been before lawmakers for a year.
-- ITAIPU WANTS TO DOLLARIZE DEBT

The government is studying a plan to convert to dollars the roughly 16 billion-real debt that the bi-national Itaipu hydroelectric project has with state-owned Eletrobras, according to the company's president.
O GLOBO
-- BRAZIL TO ALTER FEDERAL WAGE ADJUSTMENTS IN '97
The Brazilian government will change the way it grants wage adjustments to federal workers in 1997, with larger pay hikes going to employees with university degrees.
-- BRAZIL SHINES, WINS SIXTH WORLD INDOOR SOCCER TITLE
Brazil's national indoor soccer team won its sixth world championship, defeating Spain 6-4 in Barcelona.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- BRAZIL HAS INVESTED MORE IN CVRD THAN IT RECEIVED
The Brazilian government has invested in state mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) some $1.87 billion more than it has earned in dividends from the company since 1943.
-- PORTUGUESA TIES, GOES TO FINAL AGAINST GREMIO
Portuguesa on Sunday tied 2-2 with Atletico of Minas Gerais and will go to the Brazilian championship final for the first time in its history. It will play Gremio, which tied 2-2 with Goais.
-- MORE BRAZILIAN TOURISTS TRAVEL ABROAD FOR FIRST TIME
Thanks to economic stability and a proliferation of tour packages, the number of Brazilian tourists travelling abroad for the first time has doubled.
Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- James Craig, Sao Paulo newsroom 5511 232 4411
